top_stories.title: Fake academic journals are publishing AI-generated papers under real professors' names
top_stories.summary: Fraudulent academic journals are using AI to generate fake research papers attributed to real academics without their knowledge or consent. The phenomenon raises serious concerns about research integrity and the ease with which generative AI can be weaponised to produce plausible-looking but fabricated scholarly content. The trend poses significant risks to trust in academic publishing.

top_stories.title: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package
top_stories.summary: A critical security vulnerability has been discovered in a widely used open source package, putting millions of AI agents at risk. The flaw could allow attackers to compromise AI agent systems at scale. The disclosure highlights growing security concerns as agentic AI deployments become more widespread.

top_stories.title: Why the Vatican Invited Anthropic to the Pope's AI Encyclical Presentation
top_stories.summary: Anthropic's co-founder and interpretability researcher Christopher Olah was among those invited by the Vatican to attend the presentation of Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical, which addresses the power and risks of AI. The Vatican's outreach to AI safety-focused researchers reflects its effort to engage directly with leading voices on AI ethics and governance. The encyclical marks a significant moment of religious institutional engagement with AI.

top_stories.title: Rethinking organizational design in the age of agentic AI [Metered]
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review examines how the rise of agentic AI is forcing companies to reconsider how they structure teams, workflows, and decision-making. As AI agents take on more autonomous roles, traditional organisational hierarchies and processes may need fundamental redesign. The piece draws on research and executive perspectives to map out what this transition could look like in practice.

top_stories.title: The AI fight brewing inside The New York Times
top_stories.summary: The New York Times Tech Guild is pushing back against management proposals to use AI tools to monitor employee performance, with the issue becoming a flashpoint in ongoing union contract negotiations. Staff are concerned that AI-driven performance metrics could be used in disciplinary or hiring decisions. The dispute reflects broader tensions between media organisations and their workforces over AI adoption in the workplace.

further_links.title: YouTube is putting AI labels where you'll actually see them
further_links.summary: YouTube is updating its AI content labelling system to make disclosures more prominent and visible on Shorts and other content, including automatic identification of AI-generated material.

further_links.title: What Pope Leo XIV's First Encyclical Says About the Power of AI [Metered]
further_links.summary: Pope Leo XIV's debut encyclical addresses AI's societal risks and ethical dimensions, positioning the Catholic Church as a significant institutional voice in the global AI governance conversation.

further_links.title: Mid-Market Companies Lose an Average of 25% of Their AI Budget Before Seeing a Single Return, New Freshworks Research Finds
further_links.summary: New research from Freshworks finds that mid-market businesses are wasting roughly a quarter of their AI budgets before achieving any measurable return, pointing to implementation challenges and misaligned expectations.

further_links.title: The AI bubble isn't like the internet bubble
further_links.summary: Cory Doctorow at Pluralistic argues that the current AI investment bubble differs structurally from the dot-com era, with distinct implications for how and when it might deflate.

further_links.title: AI Is Taking Over the Most Cursed Job in the World [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired examines how AI is being deployed in debt collection, automating calls and negotiations previously handled by human agents, with significant implications for workers and debtors alike.

further_links.title: Take This Mandatory AI Workplace Training Right Now—or Else [Metered]
further_links.summary: Companies are increasingly mandating AI training for employees, with Wired exploring the growing pressure on workers to upskill in AI tools or face professional consequences.

further_links.title: I'm a Professional Fact-Checker. AI Is Wrong More Often Than You Think [Metered]
further_links.summary: A professional fact-checker finds that AI tools produce inaccurate or misleading information far more frequently than commonly assumed, raising questions about their reliability for research and journalism.

further_links.title: CIOs are enlisting business users to vibe code their own apps
further_links.summary: Chief information officers are increasingly encouraging non-technical employees to use AI-assisted coding tools to build their own internal applications, in a trend reshaping enterprise software development.

further_links.title: To Land a Job in AI, Try Reading Kant [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports that humanities and philosophy backgrounds are increasingly valued by AI companies seeking employees who can navigate ethics, policy, and the broader implications of AI development.

further_links.title: The Download: puncturing the AI jobs panic [Metered]
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review examines data on AI's actual impact on employment, pushing back on more alarmist predictions about widespread AI-driven job displacement.

ethan_mollick.title: Choosing to Stay Human
ethan_mollick.summary: Ethan Mollick reflects on the personal and societal choice of how much to integrate AI into daily life and work, exploring what it means to deliberately preserve human effort and experience in an age of capable AI systems. He considers the trade-offs between efficiency gains from AI assistance and the intrinsic value of doing things yourself. The post argues that staying human in some domains is a meaningful choice rather than mere technophobia.
